subject: Platform vitals checkpoint & follow-ups — May metrics
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Platform vitals checkpoint — May snapshot and follow-ups

Team,

Attached is the May platform vitals export (PDF) and a raw latency breakdown (CSV). High-level callouts from the dashboard:

- Overall uptime: 99.93% (scheduled maint windows excluded) — within SLA but trending flat month over month.
- P95 latency increased from 210ms -> 275ms for chat-generation at seq len 512; regional skew: EU regions saw a 38ms bump.
- Token-level cost per 1k tokens rose ~6% month-over-month; primary driver appears to be increased small-batch traffic and more frequent cold KV cache misses on newer models.
- Usage: steady net growth (+14% MAU), with a larger tail of low-volume tenants making lots of short requests.

Immediate asks:
1) Jonas/Markus — please validate the latency delta by region and confirm whether kernel selection changes were rolled last week (I flagged the 05/15 deploy in the dashboard).
2) Tessa — can you map the above to our QBR deck sections for "performance economics" and send a short slide (1–2) for execs by EOD Friday?
3) Vivek/Laura — align on any OKR implications (particularly around Reliability and Cost Reduction). If there are scope changes, call them out by Monday.

I'll collect replies and publish an action register. Attaching: May_vitals_dashboard.pdf, latency-breakdown.csv.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform vitals checkpoint — May snapshot and follow-ups

Irene — thanks for the snapshot and the CSV. Quick notes inline.

On Tue, May 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com> wrote:
> - P95 latency increased from 210ms -> 275ms for chat-generation at seq len 512; regional skew: EU regions saw a 38ms bump.

We saw the same in our A/B traces. Markus, we had a runtime kernel tweak pushed 05/15 for attention packing — it should have reduced memory pressure but might have changed runtime dispatch for shorter sequences. Markus, can you confirm whether the new dispatch path could introduce the extra hop? Also please enumerate which commits rolled to EU vs US (IIRC we rolled EU earlier due to capacity).

Action: Markus to produce a 1-page root-cause (by tomorrow noon) listing commits, dispatch differences, and a quick hypothesis test we can run on staging.

Also, re: cache misses — can the telemetry team provide KV cache hit-rate by tenant segment? I think that will tell us whether tenant-pattern mixing is the culprit.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform vitals checkpoint — May snapshot and follow-ups

Thanks — quick update and a proposed mitigation.

On Tue, May 22, 2027 at 10:05 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus to produce a 1-page root-cause (by tomorrow noon)…

I'll own the RCA. Preliminary findings: the 05/15 attention packing change altered the kernel selection heuristics for mixed-length batches. In practice, when short requests interleave with long requests we occasionally force a fallback path that has higher per-token overhead. I have a short runbook to reproduce this with the exact commit set; attaching a slide deck with the batching mitigation and a proposed fallback policy (batching-plan.pptx).

Proposed immediate mitigation (safe rollback NOT required):
- Force the old dispatch for mixed-length batches while we test a patch (low-risk toggle).
- Add a canary that preferentially routes EU traffic through the old path for 48 hours.

I'll run the hypothesis test on staging this afternoon and post results. If the test looks good, we can flip EU canary tomorrow and watch the p95.

Attachments: batching-plan.pptx

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Inference Engineering
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform vitals checkpoint — May snapshot and follow-ups

Thanks team — appreciate the rapid triage. A couple of items I want to call out for the QBR context:

- Cost note: the 6% token cost increase needs to be framed as a combination of transient inefficiencies (batching/misses) and sustained growth (usage). We should separate the two in the slide so Finance can see what is controllable in the next 30–60 days.
- OKR impact: Reliability OKR (RLY-2) target for P95 is <250ms by EOY. Given the current bump, we need a short mitigation plan + guardrails to ensure we don't miss quarters.

I created a short working doc to map these items to the exec QBR slides: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcDEF-OKR-map (see "Performance economics" section). Tessa — can you pull the staging numbers Markus will produce into one slide and add a callout about the OKR risk?

I'll coordinate with Finance on the cost framing and share a short note by COB.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & GTM
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Platform vitals checkpoint — May snapshot and follow-ups

Appreciate the fast responses — summary and owners below. I'll publish this to the QBR prep folder and ping execs once we have the staging test results.

Summary (action register):
- Markus: complete RCA + staging hypothesis test; produce short results note and test artifacts. Due: 2027-05-23 12:00 PDT. (attachment: batching-plan.pptx)
- Tessa: prepare 1 slide for exec QBR linking the p95 delta to cost buckets and OKR exposure. Due: 2027-05-28 EOD.
- Jonas: request KV cache hit-rate by tenant segment and surface any tenant-level patterns. Due: 2027-05-24 EOD.
- Vivek: cost framing note for Finance and OKR decision input. Due: 2027-05-23 COB.
- Irene: publish consolidated slide and email the exec readout once test results arrive. Due: 2027-05-24 EOD.

If anyone thinks these owners should shift, flag now. I'll follow up with the QBR slides link once Tessa posts them.

Thanks,
Irene
